why: Both records identify Josiah's scribe Shaphan, son of Azaliah and grandson of Meshullam, performing the same mission in Josiah's eighteenth year (2KI 22:3; 2CH 34:8). Their accounts of receiving and reading the law-book describe the same events (2KI 22:8–10; 2CH 34:15–18), and every verse on B also appears on A. A preserves the fuller compatible family evidence: Ahikam his son, Gedaliah his grandson, and Gemariah explicitly son of Shaphan the scribe (2KI 22:12; 25:22; JER 36:10). A's description of Gedaliah as king should be corrected to governor or ruler (JER 40:5; 2KI 25:22).
